notes: Synthesised from 6 parallel research passes (259 raw tells, deduped to 118). Tiers: A = flag at medium severity (artefact-class A rules may be elevated to high), B = flag at low severity / needs corroboration, C = informational only, do not implement as a user-facing flag. Kinds: lexical | phrase-regex | punctuation | structural | stylometric | model-pack. Era tags name the model generation in which the tell peaked; lexical tells decay as humans adopt AI vocabulary.

tells.tell: Density of triple-validated focal words per 1,000 words: delve(s/d/ing), showcase(s/ing), boasts, underscore(s/ing), comprehending, intricacies, intricate, surpassing/surpasses, garnered, emphasizing, realm, groundbreaking, advancements, aligns, meticulous(ly), commendable, pivotal, elucidate
tells.model_specificity: all chat models; strongest GPT-3.5/4 era, replicated across vendors
tells.era: 2023-2024 peak; decaying (delve tuned out of newer models)
tells.false_positive_risk: Each word individually is legitimate English (British/Nigerian/Indian academic use of delve; review register for commendable). Flag only cumulative density, never single hits. Human uptake post-2024 requires time decay.

tells.tell: Metaphor cluster: abstract tapestry / testament / interplay / landscape (figurative), 2+ distinct items in one document
tells.era: 2023-2026; Pew Aug 2026 confirms all more than doubled on web text
tells.false_positive_risk: Literal landscape (geography) and business idiom (competitive landscape) must be excluded; figurative tapestry is among the safest single-word tells (17,000x per Pangram).

tells.tell: Kobak 407-word style lexicon (excess_words.csv style subset): pivotal, crucial, realm, notable, noteworthy, seamless(ly), leverag-, harnessing, fostering, bolster, burgeoning, multifaceted, nuanced, transformative, unparalleled, encompass-, invaluable, streamline-, culminating, thereby, additionally, etc. Scored as cumulative density.
tells.false_positive_risk: Derived from biomedical abstracts; each word legitimate. Density-only feature. Repo licence permits reuse of data (research artefact; verify repo licence before bundling).

tells.tell: Liang top-100 AI-overused evaluative adjectives (peer-review register): versatile, innovative, noteworthy, ingenious, methodical, insightful, laudable, admirable, profound, intriguing, holistic, compelling, cogent, lucid
tells.false_positive_risk: Evaluative adjectives are the stock-in-trade of any review or testimonial; score only as co-occurring weighted cluster.

tells.tell: Liang top-100 AI-overused adverbs: meticulously, methodically, seamlessly, thoughtfully, judiciously, elegantly, compellingly, synergistically, succinctly, comprehensively, strategically, notably, aptly, hitherto, herein
tells.false_positive_risk: hitherto/herein also legalese; individual adverbs common in polished prose. Cluster-scored only.

tells.tell: Corporate buzzword verbs: leverage, utilize, harness, foster, facilitate, bolster, garner, streamline, empower, elevate, unlock, unleash, seamless, robust, game-changer
tells.false_positive_risk: VERY HIGH: pre-existing SaaS/B2B marketing jargon; leverage standard in finance, foster in social care. Combination scoring only. (Largely covered by existing tier1-3 vocab port.)

tells.tell: Promotional/travel register cluster: nestled, in the heart of, bustling, vibrant, breathtaking, rich cultural heritage, treasure trove, renowned, diverse array, must-visit, natural beauty
tells.regex: \b(nestled|in the heart of|bustling|breathtaking|rich cultural heritage|treasure trove|diverse array|must-visit)\b
tells.false_positive_risk: Identical to genuine human travel-brochure copy; upgrade weight only when register appears in genre that forbids it (encyclopedic, legal, news, technical).

tells.tell: Magic profundity adverbs: quietly, deeply, fundamentally, genuinely, famously ('quietly reshaping the industry')
tells.false_positive_risk: Feature-writing staple; too common in human prose to flag.

tells.tell: Clinical formality substitutions: individuals for people, utilize for use, in order to for to, facilitate for help, commence for start
tells.false_positive_risk: Standard register in government, legal and academic prose; ESL writers taught academic vocabulary.

tells.tell: Latinate-over-Germanic word-choice shift (demonstrate vs show, commence vs start) as corpus tendency
tells.false_positive_risk: Formal register and ESL academic training produce the same shift.

tells.tell: Formulaic paragraph-opening connectives: Additionally / Moreover / Furthermore / Subsequently / Firstly-Secondly-Thirdly
tells.false_positive_risk: Standard academic connectives; ESL convention. Flag clusters (see str-transition-stacking), not instances. Overlaps existing formulaic-openers rules.

tells.tell: Overuse of 'concrete' as adjective in argumentation (concrete evidence/examples/facts)
tells.model_specificity: unknown; noted in defensive chatbot replies
tells.false_positive_risk: Ordinary word; only notable at density in defensive replies.

tells.tell: Cross-lingual AI-word convergence: per-language top-20 AI-word lists for 34 languages (emphasize-type verbs overused in 24/34 languages)
tells.false_positive_risk: Human uptake in each language (+15.1% news-crawl drift) means time decay essential; hold for future non-English module.

tells.tell: Multilingual translationese packs: Korean 번역투, Russian канцелярит, Chinese 公文腔, Filipino, Spanish (cabe destacar que, no solo X sino también Y, hoy en día)
tells.false_positive_risk: Overlaps formal/bureaucratic native registers that predate AI by a century; per-language calibration required. Hold for non-English module.

tells.tell: Negative parallelism / contrastive negation family: 'it's not just X, it's Y', 'not only X but Y', 'X isn't the problem, Y is', 'more than just X', 'goes beyond X' — flag at 2+ occurrences per document or per 1,000 words
tells.model_specificity: all; GPT-4o/5 heavy; 'X rather than Y' variant Grok-leaning
tells.era: 2024-2026, one of the most durable tells; ~3x human rate (Pew); LinkedIn demotes it since May 2026
tells.false_positive_risk: Staple of speech-writing and ad copy (JFK); flag repetition within one document, never single use. Human uses tend to carry genuine contrast.

tells.tell: Tripled negation: 'Not X. Not Y. Just Z.' / 'No X, no Y, just Z'
tells.false_positive_risk: Ad copywriting uses it deliberately; low base rate in ordinary prose makes single hits meaningful, but keep medium not high.

tells.tell: Vague-change opener: 'In today's fast-paced/digital/modern/ever-changing world/age/landscape/era'
tells.model_specificity: all; GPT-4-era default, being trained out
tells.false_positive_risk: Human content-mill writers used it for a decade; even then it flags weak templated writing worth surfacing.

tells.tell: Hedged note-framing: 'it's worth noting that', 'it's important to note that', 'it should be noted that'
tells.regex: \bit(?:'s| is) (?:worth|important|crucial) (?:noting|to note|to remember)\b|\bit should be noted\b
tells.false_positive_risk: Academic hedging convention; one instance in a long paper is normal. Flag at 2+ per document.

tells.tell: 'stands/serves as a testament to' construction
tells.false_positive_risk: Genuine in obituaries, award speeches, sports journalism — exclude those genres or downgrade there.

tells.tell: 'plays a crucial/pivotal/vital role in (shaping)' formula
tells.false_positive_risk: Extremely common human collocation; only the full formula at density carries signal.

tells.tell: Copula avoidance: serves as / stands as / functions as / operates as / marks / represents / boasts / features where is/has fits; measurable ~10% drop in is/are frequency
tells.false_positive_risk: Copywriters trained to avoid to-be verbs; estate-agent and press-release register. Score as per-document ratio, not per-sentence.

tells.tell: Weasel authority attribution with no named source: 'Industry reports', 'Experts argue', 'Observers have cited', 'Some critics argue', 'Studies have shown', 'it is widely believed'
tells.false_positive_risk: Lazy human journalism uses identical wording — but it is a content-quality flag either way. Escalate when >50% of authority claims carry no name/link.

tells.tell: 'Despite challenges' arc: 'Despite its X, [subject] faces several challenges... Despite these challenges... continues to thrive', plus 'Future Outlook/Prospects' closers on vague optimism
tells.false_positive_risk: Business-school essay arc exists; the rigid full formula rarely occurs in human writing.

tells.tell: Undue legacy/significance framing cluster: 'marking a pivotal moment', 'enduring legacy', 'key turning point', 'indelible mark', 'setting the stage for', 'deeply rooted', 'reflects broader', 'focal point' applied to mundane subjects
tells.regex: \b(?:pivotal moment|enduring legacy|indelible mark|key turning point|setting the stage for|deeply rooted)\b
tells.false_positive_risk: Historians and obituarists legitimately discuss legacy; escalate when stacked (2+ phrases) or applied to trivial subjects.

tells.tell: Canned notability/media-coverage emphasis: 'profiled in multiple outlets', 'independent coverage', 'maintains an active social media presence'
tells.regex: \b(?:profiled in multiple|independent coverage|active social media presence|widely-read outlets)\b
tells.false_positive_risk: PR writers cite clippings; 'active social media presence' rare in human prose pre-2024.

tells.tell: Vague association scaffolding: 'associated with', 'in connection with', 'in association with' instead of defined relationships
tells.false_positive_risk: Standard in legal and police reporting; only iterative abundance signals.

tells.tell: False ranges: 'from X to Y' where endpoints are not on any real scale ('from ancient temples to bustling markets')
tells.false_positive_risk: Travel-writing cliche among humans; distinguishing fake from real ranges needs semantics, not regex.

tells.tell: Buzzword phrase pack: unlock the potential of, harness the power of, embark on a journey, at the forefront of, bridging the gap between, pave the way for, push the boundaries of, take it to the next level, navigate the complexities of
tells.regex: \b(?:unlock(?:ing)? the (?:potential|power) of|harness(?:ing)? the power of|embark(?:ing)? on a journey|at the forefront of|bridg(?:e|ing) the gap between|pav(?:e|ing) the way for|push(?:ing)? the boundaries of|navigat(?:e|ing) the complexit(?:y|ies))\b
tells.false_positive_risk: Corporate humans wrote all of these pre-2022; density and clustering separate cases.

tells.tell: Faux-insight setups: 'What most people get wrong is', 'Here's what nobody tells you', 'The part everyone misses', 'Here's the kicker', 'Plot twist:'
tells.regex: \b(?:[Hh]ere'?s what nobody tells you|[Ww]hat most people get wrong|[Hh]ere'?s the kicker|[Pp]lot twist:|[Tt]he part everyone misses)\b
tells.false_positive_risk: Growth-hacking humans invented this register on LinkedIn pre-LLM.

tells.tell: Self-posed rhetorical question answered immediately: 'The result? A platform that scales.' 'The goal? Simple.'
tells.false_positive_risk: Direct-response copywriting device; flag per-document frequency (2+).

tells.tell: Colon-reveal recurrence: 'The result: chaos.' 'The answer: simplicity.' used as default emphasis device repeatedly
tells.false_positive_risk: Genuinely good device when both halves carry weight; only recurrence signals, and human copywriters recur too.

tells.tell: 'Whether you're a X or a Y' audience-bracketing formula
tells.false_positive_risk: Content-marketing boilerplate written by humans for years; anecdotal provenance only.

tells.tell: Faux-conversational openers: 'Let's dive in', 'Let's break it down', 'buckle up', 'Ready?'
tells.false_positive_risk: Blogger house style since ~2015; weak signal amplifying others.

tells.tell: Templated analogy: 'Think of X as the Y of Z'
tells.false_positive_risk: Explainer journalism uses this constantly and well; separating generic from apt needs semantic judgement.

tells.tell: Didactic disclaimers: 'it's important/crucial to remember', 'may vary', unsolicited safety advice to an imagined reader
tells.false_positive_risk: Common in human essays/blogs; peak-2023 tell, weak on 2025+ models.

tells.tell: Narrative cliche pack: 'faced numerous challenges', 'newfound sense of purpose', 'poignant reminder', 'rich cultural heritage', 'enduring legacy'
tells.regex: \b(?:faced numerous challenges|newfound sense of purpose|poignant reminder|serves as a (?:powerful|poignant) reminder)\b
tells.false_positive_risk: Obituary and human-interest journalism cliches; multipliers so large that 2-3 co-occurring is strong evidence.

tells.tell: 'provides valuable insights into', 'complex interplay', 'a key takeaway is', 'At its core', 'To put it simply'
tells.regex: \b(?:provid(?:es?|ing) valuable insights? into|complex interplay|[Aa]t its core|key takeaways?)\b
tells.false_positive_risk: Genuine academic boilerplate predates LLMs; strongest outside academia.

tells.tell: Paired-adjective padding: 'comprehensive and thorough', 'simple and straightforward', 'complex and nuanced'
tells.false_positive_risk: Legal drafting doubles synonyms deliberately; common human filler.

tells.tell: Weak-verb constructions: 'is designed to', 'is positioned to', 'acts as a', 'marks the'
tells.false_positive_risk: 'Designed to' is accurate when describing genuine design intent.

tells.tell: 'flip the script' and 'framed by... reframed by' constructions
tells.false_positive_risk: Sports and culture journalists genuinely say it.

tells.tell: Defining a non-proper-noun title as an entity: '[Title] refers to...', 'is a curated compilation of'
tells.false_positive_risk: Textbook glossaries legitimately use 'refers to'.

tells.tell: Fake-profound kicker / aphoristic closer: 'In the end, it was never about the code.' 'The future isn't coming. It's already here.'
tells.false_positive_risk: Personal essayists earn this move legitimately; detecting the unearned variant needs semantics.

tells.tell: Species/ecosystem boilerplate: belabouring conservation status when unknown, generic 'plays a role in the ecosystem'
tells.false_positive_risk: Conservationists write about status legitimately when sourced; niche domain.

tells.tell: Habitual 'X rather than Y' reversed parallelism at high density
tells.false_positive_risk: Completely standard English; only meaningful at very high density.

tells.tell: 'comprehensive/complete/ultimate/definitive guide' title formula
tells.false_positive_risk: Human SEO writers used 'ultimate guide' titles since ~2010; predates AI.

tells.tell: Prompt-refusal / self-identification residue: 'As an AI language model', 'As a language model, I cannot... but I can', 'I'm sorry, but I can't'
tells.regex: \bAs an AI(?: language)? model\b|\bAs a large language model\b
tells.era: 2023-2024 mostly; still appears in unedited paste jobs
tells.false_positive_risk: Near zero except quoted/ironic use in articles about AI — add a quotation-context guard. (Existing chatbot-artefact rules partially cover.)

tells.tell: Knowledge-cutoff and source-gap disclaimers: 'as of my last knowledge update', 'I don't have access to real-time data', 'not widely documented', 'specific details are limited', 'in the provided search results', plus speculative fill ('likely supports...')
tells.regex: \bas of my last (?:knowledge )?update\b|\bI (?:do not|don'?t) have access to real-?time\b|\bin the provided search results\b
tells.false_positive_risk: 'my last knowledge update' has zero human usage; 'details are limited' variants legitimate for historians noting record gaps — keep those at medium. (Existing cutoff-disclaimer rules cover the core.)

tells.tell: Chat-wrapper leakage: 'I hope this helps', 'Would you like me to...', 'let me know if', 'Here is a...', 'You're absolutely right', letter-like sign-offs left in published prose
tells.regex: \bI hope this helps\b|\bWould you like (?:me to|help)\b|\b[Ll]et me know if (?:you|there)\b|\bYou'?re absolutely right\b
tells.false_positive_risk: None in published prose; normal in genuine correspondence — gate by content type (article/page, not email).

tells.tell: Sycophantic/preamble openers in published text: 'Great question!', 'Certainly!', 'Absolutely!', 'Of course!', 'I'd be happy to', prompt echo restating the request
tells.false_positive_risk: Near zero in published copy; normal in genuine conversational email — gate by surface.

tells.tell: Unfilled placeholder text: '[Your Name]', '[Specific Topic]', '[Insert X here]', 'INSERT_SOURCE_URL', 'PASTE_YOUTUBE_VIDEO_URL_HERE', access-date=2025-XX-XX
tells.false_positive_risk: Human template misuse exists but flags identically; near-zero for date/URL placeholders.

tells.tell: Exposed internal citation tokens (near-definitive, model-attributing): ':contentReference[oaicite:N]', 'oai_citation', 'citeturn0search0', 'turn0image0', 'attributableIndex' (ChatGPT); '[cite: N]', '[span_N](start_span)' (Gemini); 'grok-card data-id', 'grok_render_citation_card_json' (Grok); '【N†LX-Y】' (DeepSeek); '[attached_file:1]', '[web:1]', 'ppl-ai-file-upload' (Perplexity); ':::writing{variant=...}'
tells.model_specificity: per-token model attribution: ChatGPT / Gemini / Grok / DeepSeek / Perplexity
tells.era: 2025-2026, strings evolve per product release — version this pack
tells.false_positive_risk: Essentially none — these strings do not occur in human writing. Highest-value new category.

tells.tell: AI-tool tracking parameters in URLs: utm_source=chatgpt.com, utm_source=openai, utm_source=copilot.com, utm_source=perplexity, referrer=grok.com
tells.model_specificity: ChatGPT, Copilot, Grok, Perplexity; Gemini/Claude rarely
tells.false_positive_risk: Proves the tool touched the URL, not that surrounding prose is AI (humans fetch citations via AI) — hence medium not high.

tells.tell: Reasoning/meta leak: narrating deliberation ('the user wants... so I should...'), reviewer/submission notes embedded in the deliverable, meta-commentary about the writing task
tells.false_positive_risk: Near zero in finished prose.

tells.tell: Abrupt mid-sentence cutoff at end of text (token-limit truncation)
tells.false_positive_risk: Malformed copy/paste or truncation by humans produces the same shape.

tells.tell: Private Use Area Unicode characters (often wrapping citation tokens) and other machine-only characters in text
tells.false_positive_risk: Some icon fonts and legacy encodings use PUA; near-definitive when adjacent to citations.

tells.tell: Fabricated-reference cluster: multiple dead never-archived links, invalid ISBN checksums, DOIs resolving to unrelated papers, plausible cites with no page numbers, references defined but never used
tells.false_positive_risk: Link rot and sloppy human citing exist; several broken cites in one NEW document is the discriminator. Needs external checks (ISBN checksum is offline-computable — implementable).

tells.tell: Outdated default access-dates in citations (predating the edit by a year)
tells.false_positive_risk: Copied citations, offline drafting, batch merges.

tells.tell: Em-dash density above genre baseline (human mean ~3.2/1000 words, range 0.33-17.12; GPT-4.1 ~10.6; Claude ~9 unconstrained; ~2x web-text drift per Pew). ERA-CONDITIONAL: GPT-5.1 suppressed em dashes Nov 2025; by mid-2026 only Claude exceeds professional writers.
tells.model_specificity: Claude high through 2026; GPT-4.x historically high, suppressed from Nov 2025; Gemini/Llama low
tells.era: peak 2023-2025; decaying and now partially model-attributing
tells.false_positive_risk: VERY HIGH: professional essayists and novelists (Twain 10.13/1000); documented false-accusation smear. Density vs genre baseline only, never presence. (Existing em-dash rule: add era/model conditioning.)

tells.tell: Oxford comma at elevated rate (+63% in web text 2023-2026)
tells.false_positive_risk: House style for many publishers (Chicago, US academic); corpus-drift indicator only, never per-document.

tells.tell: Curly quotes/apostrophes in plain-text-native contexts, especially mixed inconsistently with straight quotes in one text
tells.model_specificity: ChatGPT (curly since ~mid-2025), DeepSeek; Gemini/Claude typically straight
tells.false_positive_risk: VERY HIGH unless context-gated: Word/macOS smart punctuation produces identical output. Only score in plain-text venues (CMS raw fields, code, wikitext) or on within-document inconsistency.

tells.tell: Machine-flavoured Unicode decoration in plain text: mathematical alphanumeric bold (𝗯𝗼𝗹𝗱), arrows (→) as connectors, • bullet characters pasted as text, non-breaking/narrow spaces
tells.false_positive_risk: LinkedIn Unicode-bold formatters predate AI; humans rarely type math alphanumerics elsewhere. Gate to plain-text surfaces.

tells.tell: Colon-heavy titles ('X: Why Y Matters') as habitual pattern
tells.false_positive_risk: Academic titles used colons for decades; anecdotal evidence base.

tells.tell: Deficit of human punctuation markers: fewer question marks, semicolons, parenthetical asides, contrast conjunctions (however/but/although) than genre baseline
tells.model_specificity: ChatGPT-3.5/4 validated; modern models may have shifted
tells.false_positive_risk: Plain-style human writers avoid semicolons deliberately; absence-of-X features are weak alone.

tells.tell: Sentence-final present-participle significance clauses at 2-5x human rate: ', highlighting/underscoring/reflecting/symbolizing/showcasing/emphasizing/demonstrating/ensuring/fostering/solidifying/cementing/contributing to X'
tells.model_specificity: all instruction-tuned models; hallmark of GPT encyclopedic register
tells.false_positive_risk: A single -ing tail is normal English; flag rate (e.g. 3+ per 1,000 words) with the clause asserting unearned significance.

tells.tell: Nominalisation rate 1.5-2x human (-tion/-ment/-ity noun chains: 'the implementation of the optimization of...')
tells.false_positive_risk: Bureaucratic and legal writing naturally nominalisation-heavy; needs POS tagging and per-register calibration — hold for stylometric v2.

tells.tell: Rule-of-three overuse: balanced tricolons (adjective-adjective-adjective, phrase/phrase/phrase) at ~3x human rate; flag >1 polished triad per 200 words or when every list has exactly three interchangeable items
tells.model_specificity: all; Claude and GPT noted heavily
tells.false_positive_risk: HIGH: tricolon is classical taught rhetoric; density-only metric. Human triads more often break parallelism.

tells.tell: Bold-inline-header bullet lists: '- **Term:** description' repeated for every item; label-restating bodies
tells.false_positive_risk: Technical docs and READMEs legitimately use definition lists; flag when every section is rendered this way in prose genres.

tells.tell: Mechanical boldface: key-term bolding of chosen phrases throughout flowing prose
tells.false_positive_risk: READMEs, how-tos and slide decks bold heavily; in flowing prose it is rare for humans.

tells.tell: Emoji decorating headings/bullets (🚀 ✨ 🧠 ✅ 👉 💡 🎯) in professional/neutral copy
tells.model_specificity: ChatGPT-4o-era default; Grok/Gemini too; Claude low
tells.false_positive_risk: LinkedIn/marketing humans adopted emoji headers c.2019; genre-gate (strong in encyclopedic/technical text, weak on social).

tells.tell: Title Case Section Headings where house style is sentence case
tells.false_positive_risk: AP/Chicago mandate title case; only meaningful against a known house style — needs site configuration.

tells.tell: 'X and Y' compound headings, especially the exact strings 'Awards and recognition', 'Challenges and Legacy', 'Future Outlook'
tells.false_positive_risk: Humans write awards sections; only the exact canned wordings at scale signal.

tells.tell: Heading inflation: >3 headings per 300 words; boilerplate Overview/Key Points/Conclusion scaffolding; headings containing only subheadings; skipped heading levels; first heading repeating the document title
tells.model_specificity: all markdown-trained models; Gemini most rigidly hierarchical
tells.false_positive_risk: SEO writers taught heading-dense structure for snippets pre-AI; combination of several pathologies is the signal. (Partially covered by existing uniform-sections rules.)

tells.tell: Markdown artefacts in non-markdown venues: literal **bold**, ## headings, [text](url), --- breaks, ``` fences, escaped \n or   literals in rendered pages
tells.false_positive_risk: Developers and Reddit/Discord users type markdown natively — MUST be gated to surfaces where markdown is not the native syntax (WordPress visual editor content, wikitext, plain-text fields).

tells.tell: Essay-template scaffolding imposed regardless of genre/length: signposted intro ('First we'll look at...'), three body sections, recap conclusion
tells.false_positive_risk: Students explicitly taught the template; formal reports legitimately signpost. Flag when applied where genre does not call for it.

tells.tell: Ritual conclusions: 'In conclusion / In summary / Overall / Ultimately' final paragraph restating everything already said
tells.model_specificity: all; OpenAI staff reportedly could not fully suppress
tells.false_positive_risk: School-essay convention worldwide; tell is content-free restatement, not the heading. (Overlaps existing formulaic rules.)

tells.tell: Fractal summaries / tie-back: mini-summaries at every hierarchical level, closing paragraph re-answering an answered question
tells.false_positive_risk: Essay pedagogy ('tell them what you told them'); needs semantic detection.

tells.tell: Metronomic paragraph rhythm: 3+ consecutive paragraphs of near-identical length; every paragraph 3-4 sentences ('brick wall' page)
tells.false_positive_risk: Some house styles (news wire) impose short uniform paragraphs, but even sceptics concede uniform rhythm is rarely chosen by craft writers. Easy to measure.

tells.tell: Staccato fragment spam: 3+ consecutive parallel declarative fragments under 10 words ('Real code. Working systems. Documented processes.' / 'No fluff. No filler. Just results.')
tells.model_specificity: all, esp. models asked to sound punchy
tells.false_positive_risk: HIGH: deliberate fragment beats are a real human style (ad copy, punchy blogging); protect-list known bylines.

tells.tell: Anaphora (repeated sentence openings) for manufactured emphasis
tells.false_positive_risk: Classical rhetoric; speechwriting staple.

tells.tell: Transition-word stacking: >50% of paragraphs opening with formal connectors (Furthermore, Moreover, Additionally, In addition)
tells.false_positive_risk: Formal essays and ESL academic training produce the same pattern; the majority-of-paragraphs threshold mitigates.

tells.tell: Question-form headings throughout ('What Is X?', 'How Does X Work?') with direct-answer first sentences (AEO template)
tells.false_positive_risk: VERY HIGH: deliberately taught SEO/AEO practice — human-authored AEO content trips this. Needs genre prior; do not implement.

tells.tell: Uniform FAQ/section answer lengths: every answer 2-3 sentences of near-identical length, each restating the question
tells.false_positive_risk: SEO guides explicitly teach humans this pattern for AI-citation snippets; converging from both directions.

tells.tell: Unmotivated small comparison tables where prose would do (two-column Metric/Figure table for three facts)
tells.false_positive_risk: Data journalists use tables well; 'trivial content tabulated' needs judgement.

tells.tell: Deletion-test failure / uniform emptiness: >1/3 of sentences deletable with no information loss; >50% of paragraphs with no concrete fact (name, number, date, cause, trade-off)
tells.false_positive_risk: HIGHEST FP category: corporate humans write contentless prose constantly. A concrete-noun/number density metric could ship as a quality (not authenticity) signal.

tells.tell: Absence of specific citation apparatus (et al., page numbers, direct quotes) in text that should have it
tells.false_positive_risk: Short or informal human texts also skip citations; genre-dependent absence signal.

tells.tell: Elegant variation / synonym cycling from repetition penalty: refusing to repeat a noun phrase, cycling 3+ paraphrases of one referent
tells.model_specificity: models with repetition penalty; older mainly
tells.false_positive_risk: Taught in old-school journalism; non-native writers schooled to avoid repetition. Needs coreference resolution.

tells.tell: Genre glitch: sudden promotional or sensory register intrusion into functional prose (food-blog phrase in an economics piece)
tells.false_positive_risk: Deliberate colour writing by feature journalists; needs register classification.

tells.tell: Perfect balance without commitment: every point paired with a counterpoint, no falsifiable claim; over-neat anecdotes
tells.false_positive_risk: Diplomatic and academic hedging is human too.

tells.tell: Manufactured personality / performative authenticity: fake snark ('That got old fast'), 'So I built...', manufactured before/after drama, fake war stories
tells.false_positive_risk: Indistinguishable from genuine indie-hacker blog voice without corroborating tells; document for future work.

tells.tell: Invented concept labels: coining capitalised analytical-sounding terms without rigour; grandiose stakes inflation
tells.false_positive_risk: Academics coin terms legitimately with definition and citation.

tells.tell: False agency: inanimate subjects doing human verbs as default construction ('the data tells us', 'the framework reveals')
tells.false_positive_risk: VERY HIGH: metonymy is standard English ('the market rallied'); cluster corroborator only.

tells.tell: AI edit-summary/changelog formulas: canned policy-compliance assurance, 'while preserving X / retained Y / avoided Z' procedural negatives, granular itemisation
tells.false_positive_risk: Wikipedia-specific today; generalises to git commits and CMS revision notes — future surface, not core engine.

tells.tell: Defensive comment repertoire: canned good-faith assurances + open-ended feedback requests + itemised policy lists + dismissing accusations as 'speculation'
tells.false_positive_risk: Polite non-native speakers write formally; full bundle is the tell. Platform-specific.

tells.tell: Hallucinated institutional specifics: non-existent templates/policies/shortcuts, plausible-but-wrong platform conventions, invented internal jargon
tells.false_positive_risk: New users make similar mistakes by hand; requires platform knowledge base.

tells.tell: Low burstiness / uniform sentence rhythm: sentence-length SD under ~5 words, or SD/mean below ~0.4 (humans typically 0.6-1.2), medians clustering 14-22 words
tells.model_specificity: all; weakest on frontier models (thresholds decay)
tells.false_positive_risk: SEVERE: non-native and inexperienced writers produce uniform sentences — this exact property drove the TOEFL false-positive disaster. Never alone; ship the non-native-writer caveat. (Existing flatline/burstiness rules: add thresholds and caveat.)

tells.tell: Low perplexity / high predictability under a reference LM
tells.false_positive_risk: SEVERE, with legal exposure: >50% of genuine non-native TOEFL essays misclassified. Do not implement without a non-native guard; out of scope for a rule engine anyway.

tells.tell: Lexical-diversity paradox: AI text can show HIGHER within-document TTR (thesaurus effect) while AI corpora are MORE homogeneous across documents — direction is register-dependent
tells.false_positive_risk: Contradictory directions make raw diversity unreliable standalone — existing TTR rule should compare against matched genre baseline and stay low-weight.

tells.tell: Hedging direction REVERSED vs folklore: lexical epistemic hedges DECREASED 22.8% in post-LLM scientific abstracts and LLM advice hedges ~40% less than human; the tell is formulaic note-framing, not hedge-word frequency; separately, deficit of stance markers (I think, frankly, arguably) in LLM text
tells.false_positive_risk: A naive hedge-word counter fires BACKWARDS. Do not build one. Absence-of-hedging may itself signal in scientific registers — research item.

tells.tell: Emotion skew toward joy/positivity, away from negative affect; uniform positive-evaluative register (praise without specifics)
tells.false_positive_risk: PR and brand copy deliberately positive; lazy human reviewers write the same praise sandwich.

tells.tell: Content homogenisation: multiple texts on the same topic converging on near-identical phrasing/structure
tells.false_positive_risk: Template-driven human workflows converge too; corpus-level (multi-document) feature, not per-document.

tells.tell: Sudden style shift vs an author's known writing: flawless formal prose from someone whose other output differs; wrong English variety for context; author style tracking model-era styles over time
tells.false_positive_risk: Code-switching, professional editing, non-native variety mixing common; needs per-author history — future multi-document feature.

tells.tell: Machine cleanliness: zero typos, perfect grammar, no dropped words in long informal-genre text
tells.false_positive_risk: Grammarly makes human text machine-clean; penalising cleanliness smears good writers. Listed as an INEFFECTIVE indicator — never score.

tells.tell: Inverse human signals for score REDUCTION: plain copulas (is/has), plain verbs (wrote not authored), definitive superlatives ('was the first'), informal hedges (very, perhaps), wordy constructions ('in order to', 'the fact that'), typos, first-person anecdote with irrelevant detail, text predating 30 Nov 2022
tells.false_positive_risk: n/a — implement as negative weights / protect-list to cut false accusations; pre-Nov-2022 timestamp is near-proof of human authorship.

tells.tell: Known ineffective indicators — never score: perfect grammar alone, 'bland/robotic' feel, formal register generally, transition words in isolation, unsourced content, mixed casual+formal register, Oxford comma presence, em-dash presence
tells.false_positive_risk: These ARE the false-positive traps; encode as exclusions in engine documentation and QA tests.

tells.tell: Model-specific first-word distributions (ChatGPT: as/yes/sure/here/certainly; Claude: in/from/this/based; DeepSeek: based/step/comprehensive; Gemini: my/creating/while)
tells.false_positive_risk: Very high per-instance; unverified methodology; no licence on source repo — do not copy verbatim.

tells.tell: Era-tracked vocabulary drift metadata: Era 1 (2023-mid-2024, GPT-4): delve, tapestry, testament, boasts, intricate, meticulous, garner; Era 2 (mid-2024-mid-2025, GPT-4o): align with, enhance, fostering, showcasing, highlighting; Era 3 (mid-2025+, GPT-5): emphasizing, enhance, highlighting, showcasing
tells.era: maintained through mid-2025+; check Wikipedia quarterly
tells.false_positive_risk: Powers era attribution and rule decay; a static 2023 list increasingly flags only old AI text and smears humans who absorbed the vocabulary.

tells.tell: Claude pack: em-dash rate ~5x GPT (5.4 vs 1.1 per 1,000 words; only model exceeding professional writers by mid-2026); more colons; straight quotes; richer vocabulary and varied rhythm; least formulaic structure (structural rules under-detect Claude)
tells.false_positive_risk: Evidence conflicts by version; use for attribution hints, not standalone verdicts.

tells.tell: Claude fiction/RP idiolect ('Claudeisms'): ministrations, 'audible pop', 'rivulets of', 'half-lidded eyes', 'despite herself', 'with reckless abandon', 'knuckles turning white', 'chuckles darkly', '...for now.'
tells.model_specificity: Claude specifically; separate GPT list exists
tells.false_positive_risk: Romance-genre human authors use several; fiction-lane only. Source claudeslop.yaml is AGPL-3.0 — reimplement, do not copy.

tells.tell: Fiction promptonyms: Elara (Voss/Vex), Elias Vance, Dr. Aris Thorne, Kael, Silas, Lyra, Alaric, Zephyr, 'Marcus/Sarah Chen', Whispering Woods/Pines/Hollow, Eldoria, Erebus
tells.model_specificity: cross-model (shared training data); frequency-ranked per model in slop-forensics
tells.false_positive_risk: A human could pick these names; the cluster is statistically damning in fiction. Fiction-lane only; irrelevant to marketing copy.

tells.tell: Fiction phrase slop (frequency-ranked): 'took a deep breath', 'voice barely above a whisper', 'couldn't help but feel', 'casting long shadows', 'shiver (run) down my/her spine', 'heart pounding in her chest', 'the room fell silent', 'days turned into weeks', 'a symphony of', 'maybe, just maybe', 'little did she know', 'unbeknownst to them'
tells.model_specificity: all RLHF chat models; 2,500 ranked phrases available (Apache-2.0)
tells.false_positive_risk: All are pre-existing human cliches; density per 1,000 words is the signal (SLOP_Detector graded penalty classes model this).

tells.tell: Grok idiolect: pseudo-scientific vocabulary (causal, empirical, correlate), continued 'underscore' into 2026, extreme article length, habitual 'X rather than Y'
tells.false_positive_risk: Social scientists use these words natively; attribution hint only.

tells.tell: Vendor accent classification: GPT vs Claude separable at ROC-AUC 0.96 on 18 content-free stylometric features; 5-way model attribution at 97.1% (ChatGPT/Claude/Grok/Gemini/DeepSeek), surviving paraphrase and translation
tells.false_positive_risk: Attribution assumes text IS machine-generated; applying to human text gives meaningless attributions. Roadmap item (ML, not rules).

tells.tell: Model structural dialects: ChatGPT numbered lists + bold headers + assertive declaratives; Gemini rigid hierarchical intro-body-summary; Claude least formulaic; ChatGPT+Grok emphasise broader context/legacy; Gemini+Claude more concise
tells.false_positive_risk: Vendor-blog evidence, small tests; use for calibration expectations, not scoring.

tells.tell: RLHF/preference-tuning is the root cause: annotators systematically prefer focal-word variants; instruct-tuned models emit far more formatting than base models; overt formatting collapses under 'plain prose' instructions while em dashes persist — implies layered detection (formatting tier above punctuation tier above rhythm tier) with decay expectations
tells.false_positive_risk: n/a — engine-design finding, not a surface tell.
